title: Training Preschool Teachers to Implement and Interpret Data From a Trial‐Based Functional Analysis
abstract: ABSTRACT This study partially replicated and extended Standish et al. (2023) by evaluating a modified behavioral skills training (BST) package for training preschool special educators to implement trial‐based functional analysis (TBFA). TBFA implementation fidelity, data interpretation, and data management, including application of the trial‐based ongoing visual inspection (TB‐OVI) Stop/Go criteria, were evaluated across four participants. Generalization to preschool settings and maintenance at 10‐week follow‐up were also evaluated. Participants had varying levels of prior experience with applied behavior analysis. All participants demonstrated substantial improvement across the targeted competencies from pretest to posttest. High levels of implementation fidelity were observed at posttest and generally maintained during implementation with children in preschool settings and at follow‐up, although some variability was observed across participants and conditions. Improvements were also observed in data interpretation and data management, including application of TB‐OVI Stop/Go criteria. Overall, the findings extend previous research by providing descriptive evidence of substantial improvements in a broader set of competencies relevant to conducting and evaluating TBFA following structured BST, including implementation, data interpretation, data management, and ongoing data‐based decision‐making. Implications for TBFA training and implementation in applied educational settings are discussed.
